title: Can Large Language Models Differentiate Harmful from Argumentative Essays? Steps Toward Ethical Essay Scoring
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures the ability of Large Language Models to identify and appropriately score essays containing harmful content, which is defined to include discriminatory statements against specific religions.
findings: The study found that the performance of LLMs in classifying harmful essays is significantly influenced by persona-related words. Specifically, introducing a 'Jewish' persona into the prompt altered the classification performance of all tested models, indicating the presence of biases related to this religious and ethnic term.
